a2-unit-14.14.1 Podcast:
Host: Welcome back to Green City. Last time, we talked about climate change. Today's topic is clean energy, and Dr. Mark Rivera is back with us. Welcome back!
Doctor: Thanks! It's great to be here again.
Host: So, what's the difference between fossil fuels and renewable energy?
Doctor: There are two big differences. First, renewable energy, like solar power, will never run out, but there's a limited amount of oil, gas and coal. Second, fossil fuels cause climate change, while renewable energy is much cleaner.
Host: Let's start with solar energy.
Doctor: Solar panels catch sunlight and turn it into electricity. They work in many parts of the world, and they're much cheaper now. According to the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, a home solar system in the U.S. costs more than sixty percent less than in twenty ten.
Host: But solar panels don't work at night, right?
Doctor: That's true, so many homes have a battery. The panels collect energy during the day, and the battery stores some for the night.
Host: What about wind?
Doctor: Wind turbines produce electricity when the wind blows, day or night. They're cheap to operate, although they can be noisy. And here's a fun fact: Texas produces more wind power than any other state.
Host: Texas? I thought Texas was all about oil!
Doctor: It has a lot of oil, but it has a lot of wind too.
Host: My neighbor installed a geothermal heat pump last year. What's that, exactly?
Doctor: It uses the heat in the ground to heat a house in winter and cool it in summer. Heat pumps like this are very reliable because they rarely break down. The problem is that they're expensive to install, so not everyone can have one.
Host: And hydropower?
Doctor: Hydropower uses moving water to produce electricity. It's an old idea, and it's safe and reliable. In Brazil, for example, about two thirds of the electricity came from hydropower in twenty twenty.
Host: Wow. Are there any problems?
Doctor: Yes. If it doesn't rain for a long time and the rivers get low, there isn't enough water to move the turbines.
Host: So there's no perfect solution.
Doctor: Exactly. Because every type has problems, we need a mix of clean energy.
Host: Thank you, Dr. Rivera! That's all for today. See you next time on Green City.
